status_note: First-authored 6-week race-prep block for the Concept2 2K row test. Evidence base fully sourced from whitepaper 01_aerobic_physiology.md — 28 primary citations, with 3 rowing-specific studies flagged for pre-launch URL verification.

goals.secondary: Sharpen threshold and race pace without ruining recovery
explicit_non_goals: Building the aerobic base — see Engine Builder for that

principles.rule: 80% volume at Z1/Z2, 20% at threshold or race pace.
principles.detail: Seiler 2010 polarised distribution. Race prep still respects the distribution — the 20% just concentrates in threshold + race pace rather than VO2max intervals.

principles.rule: One session per week at target 2K pace (or better) for at least 500m total.
principles.detail: Specificity of practice (Proteau 1992; Henry 1968). The 2K row is dominated by wrist-torque-analog + hip-drive coordination that only 2K-pace work develops.

principles.rule: Weeks 3-4: threshold sessions replace one Z2 session per week.
principles.detail: Joyner & Coyle 2008 — post-VO2max ceiling, threshold IS the primary metric. Threshold shifts of 3-6% over 4-8 weeks were measured by Astorino 2013 in trained cyclists; we extrapolate that range to rowing as an engineering read — see engineering_choices_flagged.

principles.rule: Last week: volume down 40-50%, intensity held.
principles.detail: Bosquet 2007 meta-analysis + Mujika & Padilla 2000 (I+II): reducing volume 40-60% while holding intensity produces the classic taper effect — ~3% performance uplift on race day. Bosquet is the stronger single-source anchor for the effect size; Mujika/Padilla cover the physiological mechanism.

principles.rule: No PR attempts outside the scheduled test days.
principles.detail: Cost-bounded. A PR attempt is a race pace effort you didn't recover from. Save it for the test.

plan_tiers.label: Foundation — 2K > 9:00
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 6: 2K time down 15-30 seconds. Threshold pace shifted 3-6%. Submax HR down 5-10 bpm at threshold.

plan_tiers.label: Progression — 2K 8:00–9:00
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: 2K down 8-15 seconds. Threshold power +5-8%. Split consistency across all four 500s.

plan_tiers.label: Push — 2K < 8:00
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: 2K down 3-8 seconds. HERITAGE-style non-response distribution begins to dominate — genetic ceiling in view.

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. If your ceiling is 2, we'll tell you upfront whether this program can deliver on its claim at that dose.

questions.label: What's your current or estimated 2K row time? (mm:ss)
questions.help: Format: mm:ss, e.g. 7:52. Type 'never' if you haven't tested a 2K on the erg.

questions.label: How familiar are you with the Concept2 erg?
Do you have a target test date? (approximate is fine)
questions.help: Format: yyyy-mm-dd. We'll place the taper accordingly.

questions.label: Do you have high blood pressure that isn't under control? (Over 160/100 at rest, or diagnosed but not on medication — uncontrolled hypertension.)
History of fainting or unexplained cardiac symptoms during hard effort?
Chest pain or shortness of breath outside normal exertion in the last 6 months?
Do you take a beta-blocker or other heart-rate-lowering medication?
questions.help: These lower your heart rate at every effort. They don't make training unsafe — but they make heart-rate targets unreachable and heart-rate retests unreadable, so we need to know.

questions.label: Are you pregnant?
questions.help: We ask because heart-rate zones stop being reliable in pregnancy — the guidance in this program is built on them.

questions.label: I consent to storing training log + symptom scores.

consent.label: I understand this is training programming, not medical advice.
I agree to stop the session if low-back pain appears during rowing (technique-driven risk).

safety_gates.block_body: Threshold and race-pace rowing pushes HR near max. Unmanaged hypertension makes that unsafe.
History of exertional syncope requires clearance before any high-intensity program.
Recent chest pain / SOB is a red flag. Defer high-intensity work pending workup.
Rowing loads the lumbar spine. Come back once the low back is settled.

safety_gates.block_title: Heart-rate targets won't apply to you
safety_gates.block_body: Beta-blockers and similar medications lower your heart rate at every effort level. The HR zones and the 90-95%-of-max targets in this program will be unreachable, and the heart-rate retest will read as no progress even when you're improving. Train by perceived effort and pace instead, and treat the HR numbers as decoration.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll go by effort and pace, not heart rate.

safety_gates.block_body: You said you're not sure. The easy work here is fine either way — the concern is the maximal 2K test and the race-pace work. A pharmacy cuff takes two minutes. Get a reading before then, and see a clinician if it's high.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: I'll get a reading before the hard sessions start.

safety_gates.block_title: Heart-rate zones won't be reliable for you
safety_gates.block_body: Resting and working heart rate both shift in pregnancy, so the HR-anchored pacing zones won't mean what they normally mean. Train by perceived effort, and take the programming to your midwife or clinician rather than to an app.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll go by effort and talk to my clinician.

phases.name: Base check · Weeks 1–2
phases.goal: Establish current 2K + submax HR baseline. Sharpen technique before overloading.
phases.rationale: Fast baseline is the honest starting point — no adaptive engine can help if it doesn't know where you started.

phases.name: Threshold build · Weeks 3–4
phases.goal: Push threshold pace up 3-6%. Add one race-pace session per week.
phases.rationale: Joyner & Coyle 2008 — threshold rises predictably at trained-athlete level with focused work; VO2max plateaus much earlier.

phases.name: Taper + test · Weeks 5–6
phases.goal: Volume down 40-50%, intensity held. Test at week 6.
phases.rationale: Mujika & Padilla 2000 — the ~3% performance uplift is bought by the taper, not by more work.
phases.block_final_week_replacements_note: In the last 7 days before the test, race-pace is replaced with easy recovery — the nervous system needs to be fresh, not primed with more race-pace exposure.

blocks.name: Zone 2 · Row
blocks.note: Sustainable pace. HR ~70-78% max. Nose breathing where possible.

blocks.name: Technique · Row
blocks.note: Slow-slide drills, feet-out, arms-only, sit-back → sequence rebuild. Cite: pace independent — quality only.

blocks.name: Threshold · Row
blocks.note: 4×8 min @ ~5-10 sec/500m over 2K pace, 2 min rest. HR 82-88% max.

blocks.name: Race pace · Row
blocks.note: 6×500m @ 2K pace, 3-4 min rest. Or 4×750m @ 2K pace + 3 sec/500m.

blocks.name: Open 2K test
blocks.note: Full 2K. Warm-up + all-out effort + cool-down. Record split, HR, RPE. This IS the retest metric.

blocks.name: Easy recovery
blocks.note: 20 min light rowing / bike / walk. Grease the groove, nothing more.

weekly_template.note: Correlated tier: all three tiers use the same layout. Foundation extends recovery; Push adds one Z2 session Sunday.
principles: Never race pace + threshold on same day.
48h between hard sessions (threshold + race pace count as hard).
Test week: race pace on Wed only, 2K on Sat, everything else easy.

immediate_actions.action: Baseline 2K in week 1 — commit to a full-effort test
Nail the catch position + drive sequence before overloading

physiological_targets.row_2k_time_seconds_change: -15 to -30 for Foundation, -3 to -8 for Push
physiological_targets.confidence: realistic for Foundation and Progression tiers; stretch for Push (genetic ceiling in view)

push.confidence: stretch — HERITAGE non-response distribution begins to dominate

session_rationale.why_polarised: Seiler 2010 — polarised 80/20 distribution outperforms threshold-dominant in trained endurance athletes over 12 weeks. Race prep respects the distribution but concentrates the 20% in threshold + race-pace work rather than VO2max.
session_rationale.why_threshold: Joyner & Coyle 2008 — post-VO2max ceiling, running / cycling / rowing threshold IS the primary trainable metric. Astorino 2013 documented ~3-6% threshold-pace shift in 4-8 wk in trained cyclists; we extrapolate that range to rowing (see engineering_choices_flagged).
session_rationale.why_race_pace_specificity: Proteau 1992 specificity + Henry 1968 — the coordination of the row stroke at 2K pace is task-specific. Only 2K-pace work develops it.
session_rationale.why_taper: Mujika & Padilla 2000 (I+II): reducing volume 40-60% while holding intensity produces a ~3% performance uplift on race day, mostly via neuromuscular / hematological restoration.

engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Race-prep block, not a base build. Shorter than the 8-12wk aerobic literature typically studies; we assume a Z2 base was built beforehand (see Engine Builder).
No RCT specifies this exact split for rowing. Extrapolated from cycling threshold-training literature.
Mujika taper literature supports 1-3 weeks; we picked the middle. Longer for older athletes may be indicated (not RCT'd for 2K row).
Match-quality effort at race pace with enough rest to preserve stroke quality. Not tested vs longer intervals for 2K prep specifically.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Astorino 2013 threshold-shift range applied to rowing
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: The 3-6% threshold shift is documented in cycling / running populations. Applied to rowing here as engineering inference — no RCT specifically for rowing threshold-shift at this dose. Would need direct citation from rowing literature to remove this flag.

Rønnestad & Hansen 2020 is the dominant contemporary short-vs-long-interval literature for trained cyclists and rowers. Not currently cited in this race-prep block — a conscious engineering choice given the 2K-specific focus, but worth noting so an auditor doesn't read the absence as an oversight.

contraindications: Unmanaged hypertension — 2K test pushes HR to max
History of exertional syncope — requires cardiac clearance
Recent chest pain / shortness of breath — workup first
Flaring low back — rowing loads the lumbar spine
adaptive_engine_hooks: day_adjustment on notes-signal 'legs dead / low back stiff' → race-pace session becomes threshold session next occurrence
amber week (≥3 amber symptom days) → drop one hard session, add one Z2
trend_slope on retest_metric.threshold_pace_500m → phase_end evaluator promotes / holds tier

onboarding_steps.title: The 0-10 scale
onboarding_steps.body_md: You'll rate recovery from prior work and life stress most mornings — both matter for a 2K test. The numbers read like this:

onboarding_steps.title: Your test date
onboarding_steps.body_md: This program peaks toward the date you set on intake. The taper week reduces volume ~45% while intensity holds — that's where the ~3% uplift comes from. Don't add extra sessions in that week.

onboarding_steps.title: Life load, today
onboarding_steps.body_md: Sleep, work, stress — anything around training. When life-load is high, Terav proposes softer targets rather than pushing splits.

currently_reads.label: Per-interval split times and total-piece splits
Per-set RPE when you log it

would_additionally_use.label: Heart rate per interval
would_additionally_use.why_it_matters: Split trend without HR is ambiguous — a slower split at lower HR is progress, a slower split at same HR is fatigue. The engine can't tell without HR.
would_additionally_use.user_action_free: Log avg + peak HR after each row.

would_additionally_use.label: Stroke rate per interval
would_additionally_use.why_it_matters: Split gains from cheating stroke rate (higher spm) look the same as gains from efficiency (same spm, faster split). Different meanings.
would_additionally_use.user_action_free: Log stroke rate per interval when the monitor shows it.

variance_source.note: HERITAGE VO2max variance extrapolated to 2K rowing performance. Anaerobic-heavy 2K response tracks aerobic VO2max response with a task-specificity multiplier — trained 2K coordination lifts even non-responders slightly.

under_dosing.copy: Threshold pace looks flat AND you've missed 20%+ of prescribed sessions. Not a ceiling — you're under-training. The engine will propose swapping a Z2 session for a race-pace session next week.

true_non_response.copy: You've hit prescribed sessions but threshold isn't moving. HERITAGE 10× variance in play. Options: (1) finish honestly, target −3 to −8 seconds on test day rather than −15; (2) extend one more 6-week block and try again; (3) accept the ceiling and move to Push-tier maintenance.

responding.copy: Threshold pace is trending faster as expected. Keep the current prescription — race-day taper will unlock the last 3-5%.

retest_metrics_mid_block.purpose: Half-way check between Week-1 base 2K test and end-block retest. Two baselines feed the classifier.
